auxiliary_passages.statement_original: For a vector $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_d)\in\mathbb R^d$ and $q>0$, we denote $|v|_q=(\sum_{i=1}^d|v_i|^q)^{1/q}$ and $|v|_\infty=\max_{1\leq i\leq d}|v_i|$. For $s>0$ and a random vector $X$, we say $X\in\mathcal L^s$ if $\|X\|_s=[\mathbb E(|X|_2^s)]^{1/s}<\infty$, and denote $\mathcal E_0(X)=X-\mathbb E(X)$. For two positive number sequences $(a_n)$ and $(b_n)$, we say $a_n=O(b_n)$ or $a_n\lesssim b_n$ (resp. $a_n\asymp b_n$) if there exists $C>0$ such that $a_n/b_n\leq C$ (resp. $1/C\leq a_n/b_n\leq C$) for all large $n$, and say $a_n=o(b_n)$ or $a_n\gg b_n$ if $a_n/b_n\to0$ as $n\to\infty$. Let $(X_n)$ and $(Y_n)$ to be two sequences of random variables. Write $X_n=O_{\mathbb P}(Y_n)$ if for $\forall\epsilon>0$, there exists $C>0$ such that $\mathbb P(|X_n/Y_n|\leq C)>1-\epsilon$ for all large $n$, and say $X_n=o_{\mathbb P}(Y_n)$ if $X_n/Y_n\to0$ in probability as $n\to\infty$.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: Distinguish finite-dimensional vector q-norms from random-variable Lq norms. The printed meaning of much-greater-than is inconsistent with the usual convention and the later threshold narrative; preserve it and record the conflict.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: The symbol $o(1)$ and $\to0$ in this theorem and the rest of the paper is in the asymptotic regime $n\wedge p\to\infty$.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: The asymptotic results concern sequences with both sample size and dimension diverging. S, neighborhood sizes, break counts and locations may also vary as specified. The Gaussian reference vector changes with n,p,b,S.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Note that in Sections 2 and 3, we assume $p=\widetilde p$, and all $A_k$, $k\geq0$, are diagonal matrices, which indicates the independence between the component processes $(\epsilon_{t,j})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$. We relax this assumption to weak cross-sectional dependence for a general $\epsilon_t$ in Section 4, and also provide the results for the same linear $\epsilon_t$ in (4) as a special case in Appendix B.4.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: The rectangular linear coefficient setup is specialized to square diagonal filters in Theorems 1-3. Theorem 4 uses its own nonlinear model and Assumptions 8-12; no appendix specialization is imported.
Theorem 2 explicitly imports this numbered rate condition only. The separate log(n)=o(sqrt(bn)) condition in Theorem 1 is not included in the reference to (15).

auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Theorem 1 implies that, for any level $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we can choose the threshold value $\omega$ to be the quantile of the Gaussian limiting distribution indicated by Theorem 1:
\[
\omega=\inf_{r\geq0}\left\{r:\mathbb P\left(\max_{bn+1\leq i\leq n-bn}Z_i>r\right)\leq\alpha\right\}.\tag{19}
\]
auxiliary_passages.resolution: This is one proposed choice of threshold. Algorithm 1 takes omega as input and Theorem 2 states its own signal and threshold rate requirements. Gaussian calibration is not required just to state the consistency theorem.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We denote the break location by $\tau_k=nu_k$, $1\leq k\leq K$, and introduce the following assumption for the identification of breaks.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: This translates rescaled times to observation-index locations. Theorem 2 binds the nearest true break k* inline. A tie rule and what is meant by estimated indices k up to K off the event K-hat=K are not supplied.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
For any time point $i$ satisfying $|i-\tau_k|\leq bn$, we define the weighted break vectors as
\[
d_i=\mathbb EV_i=\sum_{k=1}^K\left(1-\frac{|i-\tau_k|}{bn}\right)\Lambda^{-1}\gamma_k\mathbf1_{|i-\tau_k|\leq bn}.\tag{20}
\]
auxiliary_passages.resolution: This positive-sign formula conflicts with the left-minus-right estimator (3),(6) for the positive jump convention (2). It is retained as source evidence for that issue, not used to repair the theorem or add a proof-only dependency.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
We denote each element in $\mathcal Z^\diamond$ by $Z_\varphi^\diamond$, where
\[
\varphi=(i,s)\in\mathcal N,\quad\text{for }\mathcal N=\{bn+1,\ldots,n-bn\}\times\{1,\ldots,S\}.\tag{33}
\]
auxiliary_passages.resolution: The same finite product index is explicitly reused in Theorem 4. It is ambient indexing notation and does not make the general theorem depend on the earlier Gaussian covariance or linear model.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: $K\in\mathbb N$ is the number of structural breaks which is unknown and could go to infinity as $n$ increases; $u_1,\ldots,u_K$ are the time stamps of the breaks with $0=u_0<u_1<\ldots<u_K<u_{K+1}=1$

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: $b$ is a bandwidth parameter satisfying $b\to0$ and $bn\to\infty$. Without loss of generality, we assume that $bn$ is an integer.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: The shared moving-window bandwidth has integer block size, tending to infinity while its fraction tends to zero. The statistics themselves specify the admissible interior time range.

unresolved_source_conventions.note: The notation paragraph says a_n>>b_n means a_n/b_n tends to zero. This reverses the conventional reading used by the later signal and threshold discussion. Both the notation and original theorem inequalities are retained without choosing a correction.

The trend adds gamma_k at a break, whereas the local contrast and jump estimate subtract the right mean from the left. At an isolated positive jump their expectation has the opposite sign. Equation (20) nevertheless prints a positive tent-weighted gamma_k, and Theorem 2(iii) compares gamma-hat_k minus gamma_(k*). The disagreement is preserved.
The minimum starts at k=0 but the model only defines gamma_1,...,gamma_K. No gamma_0 convention is supplied. The original index range is not changed to make the condition well formed.

At Q_n=omega the algorithm enters its else branch but its strict-exceedance candidate set is empty, leaving max{k:A_k nonempty} undefined. Argmax and nearest-break ties have no explicit selection rule. Estimated quantities indexed up to true K also need an extension off the high-probability event K-hat=K. These omissions are not filled into source statements.

The jump estimate evaluates the left mean at tau-hat_k-bn and right mean at tau-hat_k+bn-1. These shifted windows can fall outside the observed range for candidate locations allowed by Algorithm 1. No boundary extension rule is supplied. The original shifts and subtraction order are retained.

unresolved_source_conventions.note: The exact centering in (7) uses coordinate variances at a fixed index. Remark 5 approximates it by 2p/(bn); the discussion after Theorem 2 instead writes an expectation at a selected random index. These expressions are not silently identified. The extracted centering and theorem use the original bar-c definition.

The displayed covariance has an overlap indicator with a free j, and no sum over j. It also invokes Xi from (11), which already includes a factor p. This does not unambiguously define the full comparison covariance. The printed expression is retained without inferring an overlap-count correction.

The numbered definition specifies coordinate subsets, while surrounding prose describes adjacent series and uses contiguity in a window-count argument. The definition itself is retained; an arbitrary set is not silently rewritten as an interval. Assumptions 6-7 and the influenced-set construction belong to Proposition 1, not a stored Theorem.

The source simultaneously puts locations in Z^v and represents them as scaled iid vectors having a density bounded above and away from zero on [0,1]^v. No rounding or alternative ambient space is specified. The density assumption is preserved as written, rather than replaced by the separate mass-to-volume discussion. Independence of random locations from the noise is not explicitly stated.

The source calls each interval an interval on Z and then assigns its rectangle Lebesgue volume. A literal finite lattice rectangle has zero Lebesgue measure; a continuous enclosing rectangle would be a different interpretation. The source does not state that change of interpretation. Its mass comparability condition is retained with the full definition.

Equation (5) uses sigma_j squared for the long-run variance; equation (44) instead defines sigma(l)=sigma(l,l) as the variance, but later inverses and the correlation ratio use sigma(l) as if it were a standard deviation. The general formulas are preserved with no square-root correction. Unlike (5), the general setup does not explicitly repeat a uniform positive variance bound.

The nonlinear representation uses ell-prime in Z^v, but both displayed coupled versions use Z. The replacement rule is stated only for i>=0 although the process uses an entire negative-time history. The double-star rule replaces i=0 OR s=0, not only their intersection. These source domains and logical conditions are retained.

The piecewise covariance formula covers only zeta>0 and does not state its diagonal or other same-time entries. The overlap indicator requires both spatial indices in the intersection of the two rectangles, as printed. No zero-lag limit or different overlap weights are supplied by the census. The detailed evaluation is referred to appendix Lemma 15, which was not read.

Theorems 1 and 3 explicitly exclude dependence of the implicit constant on n,p,b; Theorem 4 additionally excludes S. These exact clauses are retained, as are the different error rates. The Gaussian comparison laws are finite vectors depending on the asymptotic parameters, not a single fixed limiting distribution.

The variance estimator is referred to Appendix A.1 and the detailed general covariance evaluation to Lemma 15 in Appendix C. No appendix body was inspected. The census preserves the known-scale main-text statistic and records the covariance specification omissions rather than importing those details.
